steps.label: Revision 2: Arrays and Searching
steps.content:
Algorithms

Revision 2: Arrays and Searching

Year 8

  • Today: read an array, then trace a search.
  • Then: practice questions like the test.
  • Next lesson: the assessment.
Think → Pair → ShareWhy keep many values in one array, and not in many variables?Show the answer

One name holds them all. One loop can visit every value. Ten variables would need ten lines.

steps.label: Key Words
steps.content:
Key Words

Think → Pair → ShareLook at Marks[2]. Which part is the name? Which part is the index?Show the answer

Marks is the name of the array. 2 is the index: the position.

DECLARE Marks : ARRAY[1:4] OF INTEGERmake an array: 4 values, one name
indexthe position number, in [ ]
Marks[2]the value at index 2
DECLARE Found : BOOLEANa BOOLEAN stores TRUE or FALSE
linear searchcheck each item, one at a time, from index 1
trace tablewrite each new value when it changes

steps.label: Arrays: Index and Value
steps.content:
Arrays: Index and Value

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what does line 6 output? Why is it not 3?Show the worked answer

Output: 5.

3 is the index, the position. Go to index 3 and read the value there: 5.

1  DECLARE Marks : ARRAY[1:4] OF INTEGER
2  Marks[1] <- 6
3  Marks[2] <- 9
4  Marks[3] <- 5
5  Marks[4] <- 8
6  OUTPUT Marks[3]

Marks

Index1234
Value6958
  • The top row is the index (the position).
  • The bottom row is the value.
  • Marks[3]: go to index 3, read the value.
  • Index 1 is the first item.

Each time round, Index is the next position, so line 5 adds the next value: 4, then 9, then 2.

Prices

Index123
Value492
1  DECLARE Total : INTEGER
2  DECLARE Index : INTEGER
3  Total <- 0
4  FOR Index <- 1 TO 3
5    Total <- Total + Prices[Index]
6  NEXT Index
7  OUTPUT Total
  • Index goes 1, 2, 3.
  • Line 5 uses Prices[Index]: the value at that index.
  • So each time round, it adds the next value.
  • In a trace table, write a new row each time a value changes.

steps.label: Linear Search: Check Each Item
steps.content:
Linear Search: Check Each Item

Think → Pair → SharePredict: the user types Dog. What is output? At which index does it match?Show the worked answer

Output: Found.

Index 1: Cat is not Dog. Index 2: Dog = Dog, so line 8 sets Found to TRUE. After the loop, Found = TRUE, so line 12 runs.

1  DECLARE Search : STRING
2  DECLARE Found : BOOLEAN
3  DECLARE Index : INTEGER
4  INPUT Search
5  Found <- FALSE
6  FOR Index <- 1 TO 3
7    IF Pets[Index] = Search THEN
8      Found <- TRUE
9    ENDIF
10  NEXT Index
11  IF Found = TRUE THEN
12    OUTPUT "Found"
13  ELSE
14    OUTPUT "Not Found"
15  ENDIF

Pets

Index123
Value"Cat""Dog""Fish"
  • Found starts as FALSE (line 5).
  • The loop checks each item, from index 1.
  • A match sets Found to TRUE (line 8).
  • After the loop, line 11 checks Found.
